messages:
elena: Hey runtime team — finalizing webinar + launch blog. Need a tiny, reproducible bench bundle we can cite.

Short asks: heatmap comparing coldstart vs steady (per-request), 50/95/99 latencies, tokens/sec, and $/1k tokens for fp16 and quantized int8 variant. Include the exact command, env (drivers/kernels), and the sample payloads.

matt: Got it. Which model + config? batch/concurrency matrix?

elena: Use redwood/3b-compat-v1 (prod-like). Run batch sizes 1 and 8; concurrencies 1 and 16. Sequence lengths: 32 / 192 / 1024. Per-request percentiles.

sophie: Also ask to log warmup traces and note any KV-cache priming. Marketing will publish a single slide and a short note on caveats.

andy: We can do a focused smoke tomorrow AM. Plan: 3 warmup runs, then 150 samples per cell. Capture 50/95/99, GPU util, and stderr on any kernel warnings. We'll push artifacts to /internal/bench/artifacts/<id>.

elena: Sample set: https://gist.example.com/redwood/webinar-samples. Use "webinar-clean" prompts only.

matt: Also output a normalized chart vs hosted fp16 baseline and raw CSV. Sophie: do you need CI on these numbers?

sophie: CSV + normalized chart + one PNG for the slide. If quantized shows instability at 1024, call that out with exact stderr and kernel versions. Deadline Thu 18:00 PT.

andy: Repro block we'll attach:
```
# smoke reproduce (example)
curl -sS -X POST https://runtime.internal.redwood/api/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/3b-compat-v1","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":64,"batch":1}'
```

runtime-bot: Job queued: run_id=job-2026-1718-01, ETA ~2h. Logs: /internal/bench/runs/job-2026-1718-01

matt: I'll capture commit hash, CUDA, driver, and kernel selection in env.txt. If int8 behaves nondeterministically, we'll include stderr and a conservative note.

andy: Target: run Wed EOD, artifacts Wed night, marketing picks Thu morning. If any run fails, we'll surface minimal conservative wording for the press.

elena: Perfect — please ping @matt and @andy with updates. Keep the slide simple: one heatmap (coldstart vs seqlen) + 2-col chart (throughput vs $/1k). Thanks!
